All context gathered. Here is the Phase E6 architecture. Two genuine contradictions surfaced (Esc semantics, rehearsal form), so I am asking them first with defaults, and the design below proceeds on those defaults.

## QUESTIONS FOR USER
- Q1: Esc semantics conflict: `consoleStore.ts` documents "Esc clears the lookup query" while the E6 brief says "Esc = clear selection". Recommended default: layered dismiss, Esc cancels an open typed-shock gate first, then clears the lookup query, then resets the whole console (query is already empty at that point, so the last step equals clear selection plus clear twist). This matches the between-judges ritual and needs no new store action.
- Q2: Rehearsal form: an in-app timed dock (small component driving the real console through 5 scripted steps) vs a printed script only (section of the paper sheet). Recommended default: in-app dock with the printed script as the named cut line if the hour runs short (the script data module ships either way).

---

## Architecture: Judge Mode (E6) - Phase 6 of 7

### Overview
E6 turns the console into a live judging instrument: one authoritative keyboard map exported from `src/lib/judgeMode.ts` and wired by a thin window-level adapter hook, an edge-account guard rebuilt to read the E1 profile flags (with contextual copy for the layoff-on-pensioner case), a lean scripted rehearsal dock over 5 frozen golden-fixture accounts, and a one-page printable judge sheet in `public/` as the laptop-dead fallback. All rules stay pure functions in `src/lib`; components only wire listeners and markup, and the adapter fires exactly one existing atomic store action per keystroke.

### Phase Scope
Covers: keyboard shortcuts and their context rules, edge-account guards and operator script lines, rehearsal mode and its data, paper fallback artifact. Connects to: E2 (store actions and DOM seams `id="account-lookup"`, `data-preset`, `type="button"` are consumed, not changed; the reserved key map comment in `consoleStore.ts` is superseded by a pointer to the judgeMode registry), E5 (Atlas above console, `id="atlas"` / `id="console"`; the single window listener works across both sections), E4 (reads `planMath`/`planText`/`PlanCard` for context only, zero edits to those files or README.md), E7 (ReceiptBadge untouched; only a receipt link slot in the bar is possible later). Out of scope: any store action changes, any shock math, any E4 plan content.

### Component Breakdown

| Component | Responsibility | File |
|-----------|---------------|------|
| Key registry + resolver | Single authoritative key table, pure context-aware resolution, modifier policy | `src/lib/judgeMode.ts` (rewrite) |
| Edge guard | Pure guard report from `AccountProfile` flags + live twist context + unknown id | `src/lib/judgeMode.ts` (rework `edgeGuard`) |
| Random account picker | Pure "safe demo" pool and seeded pick for the N key | `src/lib/judgeMode.ts` (new `pickRandomAccount`) |
| Rehearsal script | Pure data: 5 steps over the golden fixture accounts, timer verdict | `src/lib/rehearsal.ts` (new) |
| Dispatcher + key listener | Thin DOM adapter: maps `JudgeAction` to existing store actions and focus effects | `src/components/judge/useJudgeShortcuts.ts` (new) |
| Guard derivation hook | One `useMemo` over `{bundle, selectedId, twist}` calling `edgeGuard`, shared by bar and chips | `src/components/judge/useEdgeGuard.ts` (new) |
| Judge chips | Judge-facing short-label chips near the verdict, full message on hover/aria | `src/components/judge/GuardChips.tsx` (new) |
| Judge bar (extend) | Renders the 9 bindings as buttons via the shared dispatcher; rehearsal toggle; paper sheet link | `src/components/judge/JudgeBar.tsx` (extend) |
| Rehearsal dock | Timed dry run UI: run step, answer button, elapsed vs 2.0 s target | `src/components/judge/RehearsalDock.tsx` (new) |
| App shell | Mounts `useJudgeShortcuts`, `JudgeBar` (bottom), `RehearsalDock` | `src/App.tsx` (extend) |
| Console shell | Mounts `GuardChips` as one new sibling line after `cp-grid` | `src/components/console/ConsoleView.tsx` (one line) |
| Paper sheet | Standalone printable one page: definitions, formula, bands, worked example, guards, keys | `public/judge-sheet.html` (new) |
| Store comment | Reserved key map block replaced by a pointer to `JUDGE_SHORTCUTS` | `src/state/consoleStore.ts` (comment only) |

### Data Flow

```
window keydown (App mounts useJudgeShortcuts once)
  -> adapter: isTextEntry(target)? isComposing? repeat?   (DOM facts only)
  -> resolveJudgeKey(event, context)                      [pure, src/lib/judgeMode.ts]
       context = { inTextEntry, typedGateOpen }
  -> JudgeAction | null
  -> dispatchJudgeAction(action)   (same function serves JudgeBar button clicks)
       twist n      -> useConsole.applyPreset(SHOCK_PRESETS[n-1].id)
       reset_twist  -> useConsole.resetTwist()
       reset_all    -> useConsole.resetAll()
       focus_lookup -> document.getElementById('account-lookup').focus()
       dismiss      -> cancelTypedShock() | setQuery('') | resetAll()   (layered)
       random       -> pickRandomAccount(bundle, {rng}) -> selectAccount(id)
  -> store update (one atomic action per keystroke, E2 contract intact)
  -> ConsoleView derivation useMemo (unchanged: applyTwist, verdictBand, forecast, plan)
  -> useEdgeGuard(): edgeGuard({profile, jobLossActive, knownAccountIds})
       -> GuardChips (chips row under cp-grid) + JudgeBar guard strip (full messages)
RehearsalDock "Run step" -> same store actions (selectAccount + applyPreset), stopwatch local
```

### File Structure

| File | Purpose | Changes |
|------|---------|---------|
| `src/lib/judgeMode.ts` | Registry, resolver, guard, picker, copy tables | Rewrite: 9-binding `JUDGE_SHORTCUTS`, `resolveJudgeKey`, `edgeGuard` over `AccountProfile`, `pickRandomAccount`, delete `GUARD_MIN_ROWS`, `account_prev/next`, old flag set |
| `src/lib/judgeMode.test.ts` | Unit tests | Rewrite to the new registry, context matrix, guard copy, picker determinism |
| `src/lib/rehearsal.ts` | `REHEARSAL_SCRIPT`, `REHEARSAL_TARGET_MS`, `rehearsalVerdict` | New |
| `src/lib/rehearsal.test.ts` | Coverage + artifact pinning | New |
| `src/components/judge/useJudgeShortcuts.ts` | `useJudgeDispatcher`, `useJudgeShortcuts` | New |
| `src/components/judge/useEdgeGuard.ts` | `useEdgeGuard` shared derivation | New |
| `src/components/judge/GuardChips.tsx` | Chip row near verdict | New |
| `src/components/judge/RehearsalDock.tsx` | Timed dry run panel | New |
| `src/components/judge/JudgeBar.tsx` | Bar | Extend: props `onToggleRehearsal`, `rehearsalOpen`, `paperHref`; trailing link + toggle button |
| `src/components/judge/JudgeBar.test.ts` | Bar tests | Extend: 9 bindings, toggle, paper link |
| `src/components/judge/judgeShortcuts.smoke.test.ts` | jsdom adapter smoke (style of `console.smoke.test.ts`) | New |
| `src/App.tsx` | Shell | Extend: `useJudgeShortcuts()`, `<JudgeBar>` bottom bar with `onAction={dispatch}`, `<RehearsalDock>` |
| `src/components/console/ConsoleView.tsx` | Console shell | One line: `<GuardChips guard={useEdgeGuard()} />` after `cp-grid` (or extract to a prop-free child if the E4 merge conflicts) |
| `src/state/consoleStore.ts` | Store | Comment only: reserved map block becomes "see `JUDGE_SHORTCUTS` in src/lib/judgeMode.ts" |
| `public/judge-sheet.html` | Printable fallback | New: standalone inline-CSS one pager |
| `docs/competition-day-runbook.md` | Runbook | Add the sheet link to the Sunday demo row and the "Offline booth" risk fallback cell |
| `docs/judge-sheet.test.ts` (optional, in `src/`) | Asserts sheet numbers | New, cut line 2 |

### Technology Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Why | Alternative Rejected | Trade-off |
|----------|--------|-----|---------------------|-----------|
| Key map source of truth | One `JUDGE_SHORTCUTS` table in `src/lib/judgeMode.ts`; `consoleStore` comment points at it | The brief names judgeMode as owner; one table means the bar, the tests, and the sheet cannot drift | Keeping two maps with a sync comment | The E2 comment wording (Esc, arrows) is superseded; recorded in decisions.md |
| Key set | Exactly the reserved map: `1`-`4`, `r`, `Shift+R`, `/`, `Esc`, `N` (9 bindings) | Reserved map is the approved contract; arrows removed (they conflicted with the map and with text selection via Shift+arrows) | Keeping ArrowLeft/ArrowRight walking | Account browsing loses keyboard stepping; lookup typing and N cover the ritual |
| Modifier policy | Reject ctrl/meta/alt always; `shiftKey` allowed only for bindings with `allowShift` (only `Shift+R`) | Shift alone never triggers browser shortcuts; `Shift+R` needs it; `Shift+4` types `$` so numbers cannot collide | Blanket modifier reject (killed Shift+R) | Caps Lock `R` also fires reset-all; documented, harmless |
| Listener placement | Pure `resolveJudgeKey` in lib + `useJudgeShortcuts` window listener mounted in `App` | Window scope works across Atlas and console (E5 layout); pure rules unit test without DOM; layering holds | Listeners in ConsoleView (misses Atlas focus, remount churn); listeners in the store module (DOM in state layer) | One global listener must own the focus guard carefully |
| Typed-shock interplay | While `typedStatus` is `reading` or `pending`, only `Esc` resolves; text-entry focus suppresses everything except `Esc` | `applyPreset` would silently `retireTypedParse` and drop the judge's sentence chips; typing `1` in the lookup is an id digit, not a shortcut | Allowing resets during the gate | The confirm button is auto-focused (a button), so the gate-open rule is required, not just the focus rule |
| Guard source | Read `profile.flags` (E1 artifact) instead of re-deriving thresholds | E1 flags are verified field-by-field by `scripts/engine/verify.py`; kills the dead `GUARD_MIN_ROWS = 6` and its wrong message | Keeping `rowCount < 18` re-derivation in TS | Guard trusts the artifact; drift is caught by the existing engine verify, not duplicated in TS |
| Guard placement | Full messages in the judge-facing `JudgeBar` strip (operator), short chips near the verdict (`GuardChips`) | Operator needs the sentence, judges need the glance; two renders of one pure `GuardReport` via `useEdgeGuard` | Chips inside ShockPanel/PlanCard (merge risk with E4) | Chips sit under `cp-grid`, a few pixels from the badge rather than inside it |
| N picker | Pure `pickRandomAccount` with a "safe demo" pool, injectable `rng` | Never embarrasses the operator; deterministic under test and rehearsal | Uniform random over 4500 ids | Extreme accounts are unreachable via N (still typed by judges, guarded) |
| Rehearsal | Pure `rehearsal.ts` script + lean `RehearsalDock` with stopwatch | The live ritual is timing muscle memory; the data module survives the UI cut | Full game-like scoring, persistence | No history or scoring beyond a per-step green/amber/red label |
| Paper fallback | `public/judge-sheet.html`, standalone, `@media print`, linked from the runbook | Ships with Pages, prints offline, needs no build step; runbook "Offline booth" row expects everything bundled | `docs/` markdown (not printable to one page without tooling); generated PDF in repo (binary churn) | Hand-copied numbers from `golden_fixtures.json`; an optional test pins them |

### Interfaces

```ts
// src/lib/judgeMode.ts (rewrite)
export type PresetIndex = 1 | 2 | 3 | 4

export type JudgeAction =
  | { kind: 'twist'; preset: PresetIndex }
  | { kind: 'reset_twist' }
  | { kind: 'reset_all' }
  | { kind: 'focus_lookup' }
  | { kind: 'dismiss' }
  | { kind: 'random_account' }

export interface ShortcutBinding {
  id: string
  keys: readonly string[]        // KeyboardEvent.key values, first is displayed
  label: string                  // sentence case, shown in the bar
  action: JudgeAction
  allowShift?: boolean           // only Shift + R
  allowInTextEntry?: boolean     // only Esc
}

export const JUDGE_SHORTCUTS: readonly ShortcutBinding[]   // 9 entries, bar order

export interface ShortcutKeyEvent {
  key: string
  ctrlKey?: boolean
  metaKey?: boolean
  altKey?: boolean
  shiftKey?: boolean
  repeat?: boolean
}

export interface JudgeKeyContext {
  inTextEntry: boolean           // input, textarea, select, or contentEditable
  typedGateOpen: boolean         // typedStatus is reading or pending
}

export function matchShortcut(
  event: ShortcutKeyEvent | null | undefined,
  shortcuts?: readonly ShortcutBinding[],
): JudgeAction | null                                   // registry match only

export function resolveJudgeKey(
  event: ShortcutKeyEvent | null | undefined,
  context: JudgeKeyContext,
  shortcuts?: readonly ShortcutBinding[],
): JudgeAction | null                                   // context rules on top

// Guard (reworked)
export const GUARD_FLAG_ORDER = [
  'unknown_account', 'pensioner', 'zero_income', 'thin_history',
  'negative_buffer', 'defaulted_loan', 'no_loan', 'zero_household_bills',
] as const
export type GuardFlagId = (typeof GUARD_FLAG_ORDER)[number]

export interface GuardFlag {
  id: GuardFlagId
  label: string        // chip text, e.g. "thin history"
  message: string      // full operator sentence, no dash glyphs
}

export interface GuardInput {
  accountId?: string | null
  knownAccountIds?: readonly string[] | null
  profile?: AccountProfile | null        // from src/data/profiles (type only)
  jobLossActive?: boolean                // the live twist has jobLoss true
}

export function edgeGuard(input: GuardInput | null | undefined): GuardReport
// GuardReport unchanged: { accountId, flags, needsCare }

// Random account (new)
export function randomAccountPool(profiles: readonly AccountProfile[]): AccountProfile[]
export function pickRandomAccount(
  artifact: ProfilesArtifact,
  options?: { excludeId?: string | null; rng?: () => number },
): string | null
```

```ts
// src/lib/rehearsal.ts (new)
export interface RehearsalStep {
  id: string
  accountId: string
  presetId: PresetId                       // from src/lib/shockPresets
  expectFlags: readonly GuardFlagId[]
  scriptLine: string                       // what the operator says while the numbers run
}
export const REHEARSAL_TARGET_MS = 2000
export const REHEARSAL_SCRIPT: readonly RehearsalStep[]
export function rehearsalVerdict(elapsedMs: number): 'fast' | 'ok' | 'slow'
// fast < 2000, ok < 4000, slow otherwise
```

```ts
// src/components/judge/useJudgeShortcuts.ts (new)
export function useJudgeDispatcher(options?: { rng?: () => number }): (action: JudgeAction) => void
export function useJudgeShortcuts(options?: { rng?: () => number }): void
```

```ts
// src/components/judge/useEdgeGuard.ts (new)
export function useEdgeGuard(): GuardReport | null   // null before boot
```

### Authoritative Key Table (ships in the bar, the sheet, and the tests)

| Key | event.key | Action | Effect | Context rules |
|-----|-----------|--------|--------|---------------|
| `1` | `1` | twist preset 1 | `applyPreset('layoff')` | Suppressed in text entry and while the typed gate is open |
| `2` | `2` | twist preset 2 | `applyPreset('cost_spike')` | Same |
| `3` | `3` | twist preset 3 | `applyPreset('emergency_repair')` | Same |
| `4` | `4` | twist preset 4 | `applyPreset('combo')` | Same |
| `r` | `r` | reset twist, keep account | `resetTwist()` | Same |
| `Shift+R` | `R` | reset everything | `resetAll()` | Same; the only binding tolerating shift. Caps Lock `R` also fires it |
| `/` | `/` | focus lookup | `#account-lookup`.focus(), preventDefault (Firefox quick find) | Suppressed in text entry and while the gate is open |
| `Esc` | `Escape` | layered dismiss | gate open: `cancelTypedShock()`; else query non-empty: `setQuery('')` (+ blur); else selected or shocked: `resetAll()`; else no-op | Active everywhere, including text entry (the only key exempt from the focus guard) |
| `N` | `n` | pseudo-random account | `selectAccount(pickRandomAccount(bundle))` | Suppressed in text entry and while the gate is open; key repeat ignored |

Esc layered rule (the Q1 default): it dismisses the innermost layer first, so the operator can never lose a typed sentence to a stray keypress, and between judges two presses (or one when no query) return the console to the empty state. This supersedes the `consoleStore` comment wording.

### Guard Copy Table (no dash glyphs anywhere)

| Flag id | Fires when | Chip label | Operator message (bar) | Operator script line (rehearsal) |
|---------|-----------|------------|------------------------|----------------------------------|
| `unknown_account` | id missing or not in `bundle.byId` | unknown id | Account id is not in the loaded profile set | "That id is not in the 4,500 account index, let me retype it." |
| `pensioner` (idle) | `flags.pensioner` | pension income | Pension income account: money in is pension, not wages | "Income here is pension, so the money in line reads differently." |
| `pensioner` (layoff twist live) | `flags.pensioner && twist.jobLoss` | pension vs layoff | Layoff twist simulated against pension income: this account has no wage to lose, read the verdict as a stress test | "Good catch: this customer's income is pension, so the layoff card is a stress test on fixed income. Their real risk is bills up, not job loss." |
| `zero_income` | `flags.zero_income` | zero income | Zero income: money in is 0, so the layoff and EI framing does not apply | "Money in is zero here, so I read the shock as a spending side stress." |
| `thin_history` | `flags.thin_history` (row_count under 18, E1 definition) | thin history | Thin history: fewer than 18 monthly rows, so the baseline medians rest on a short window | "Short history, so I treat the baseline as low confidence." |
| `negative_buffer` | `flags.negative_buffer` | negative buffer | Savings buffer is below zero: the baseline already reads 0.0 months of runway | "Buffer is already below zero, so the plan is recovery first." |
| `defaulted_loan` | `flags.defaulted_loan`, message varies on `loan.status` | defaulted loan | status D: Loan in arrears (status D): the account still pays a loan it is behind on. status B: Loan defaulted and closed (status B): no payment runs, so the loan levers do not apply | D: "This loan is running and in arrears, so deferral is exactly the intervention." B: "This loan already defaulted and closed, so there is no payment to defer." |
| `no_loan` | `loan_payment_cents === 0` | no loan | No running loan payment: the loan deferral lever does not apply | "No loan payment here, so I skip the loan lever and say why." |
| `zero_household_bills` | `household_bills_cents === 0` | zero bills | Household bills are 0: a bills shock cannot move this account | "Bills are zero here, so a rent shock cannot land; I would swap to the repair card." |

Rules: flags are advice, never gates (`selectAccount` accepts any known id regardless of flags, the hard constraint "any account must work" is untouched). Canonical order is `GUARD_FLAG_ORDER`, the pensioner message variant is decided by the live twist, and every message keeps the repo no-dash content rule (a `judgeMode.test.ts` case already scans for dash code points; keep it). This table backs the shipped `docs/devpost.md` claim: thin history, negative buffer, zero bills, and missing loans all flag before a judge finds them.

### Rehearsal Spec

Format: scripted dry run, 5 steps, timed, no stakes, driven through the real store so the operator practices the actual keystrokes. Target: 2.0 s from step reveal to "Answered" click (`REHEARSAL_TARGET_MS`); labels `fast` / `ok` / `slow` at 2 s / 4 s.

| Step | Account | Why this account | Twist | Expected flags | Expected read |
|------|---------|------------------|-------|----------------|---------------|
| 1 | `68257` | Golden fixture: odd median, running loan C, clean | `layoff` (1) | none | Fair skies 9.8 months falls to Storm warning 1.8 months |
| 2 | `23838` | Golden fixture: half cent tie in I, `no_shortfall` branch | `cost_spike` (2) | none | Verdict stays Clear, buffer absorbs |
| 3 | `98952` | Golden fixture: pensioner, no loan | `layoff` (1) | `pensioner` (layoff variant), `no_loan` | Stress-test framing, loan lever skipped |
| 4 | `49900` | Golden fixture: thin history (17 rows) and zero income | `combo` (4) | `thin_history`, `zero_income` | Caveat spoken before the number |
| 5 | `42988` | Golden fixture: defaulted loan status D, negative buffer | `emergency_repair` (3) | `defaulted_loan` (D variant), `negative_buffer` | Baseline already 0.0, recovery plan |

Coverage: all five E1 flags fire at least once, all four presets fire once except `layoff` (twice, needed for the pensioner variant), every runway branch appears across the fixtures. Candidate selection criteria (recorded for any future re-pick): ids come from `scripts/engine/golden_fixtures.json`, which is hand-verified and pinned by both pytest and vitest; `rehearsal.test.ts` asserts each step's id exists in the shipped `profiles.json` with exactly the expected flags, so artifact drift fails a test and names the step. If a rebuild ever invalidates an id, re-pick from `meta.edge_flag_counts` smallest buckets first (`zero_income` 14, `negative_buffer` 23, `defaulted_loan` 45, `thin_history` 377, `pensioner` 740), preferring fixture-frozen ids so the paper sheet example stays pinned.

UI (`RehearsalDock`): opened from a toggle in `JudgeBar`; shows step n of 5, the judge card sentence (from `presetById`), the script line, a "Run step" button (selects the account and applies the preset via the store), and an "Answered" button that stops the stopwatch and prints the verdict label. Closing resets the counter. No persistence, no network, no score history.

Cut line (Q2 default): if the hour runs short, cut `RehearsalDock.tsx` and keep `rehearsal.ts` plus a printed script block in the judge sheet. The data module is cheap and the sheet prints it.

### Paper Fallback Spec (`public/judge-sheet.html`)

Purpose: the rehearsed fallback when the laptop dies or the venue network stalls (runbook risk table "Offline booth" expects everything bundled locally with fixture labels; `docs/devpost.md` promises a graceful fallback). Standalone HTML, inline CSS, `@media print` sized to one US Letter page, no build step, no JS. Linked from `docs/competition-day-runbook.md` (Sunday demo row and the Offline booth fallback cell) and printable from the live site (`/judge-sheet.html`). Readme linking is deliberately out of scope (concurrent agent owns README.md).

Sections, in order:
1. **Header**: "Resilience Weather Station, judge sheet", competition name, "synthetic demo data label applies to cached fixture figures".
2. **The six definitions**: I, F, S, B, H, P exactly as `docs/tangerine-challenge.md` lines 52 to 59.
3. **Runway formula and rounding**: the branch formula (challenge doc lines 63 to 69), ROUND_HALF_UP to 1 decimal, cap at 120.0.
4. **Worked example** (numbers hand-copied from `scripts/engine/golden_fixtures.json` account `68257`, whose "steps" block is visible workings): I = 650,326c, S = 716,084c, B = 643,785c, H = 430,672c, P = 284,493c, gap = 65,758c, baseline deci = (20 x 643785 + 65758) // (2 x 65758) = 98, so 9.8 months. Layoff card: income_after = round(0.55 x I) = 357,679c, gap_after = 716,084 - 357,679 = 358,405c, deci = (20 x 643785 + 358405) // (2 x 358405) = 18, so 1.8 months. Fair skies becomes Storm warning.
5. **Verdict bands**: the five `verdict.ts` bands with their threshold strings (critical: buffer gone or under 1.0 month; storm warning 1.0 to 2.9; watch 3.0 to 5.9; fair skies 6.0 to 11.9; clear 12.0 and up or no shortfall).
6. **Twist card arithmetic**: `income_after = 0.55 x I` (layoff), `spending_after = S + 0.15 x H` (bills up 15%), `one_off_costs = 1.0 x S` (furnace), combo is layoff plus bills; duration is display only.
7. **Guard one-liners**: the chip labels plus one phrase each from the guard copy table.
8. **Key table**: the authoritative 9 rows.
9. **Rehearsal script**: the 5 steps (account, card, expected flags), so the drill survives a dead laptop.

Content rules: no em dash, en dash, minus sign, or double hyphen anywhere (use `x`, `+`, and words); money shown in cents and dollars; every figure traceable to `golden_fixtures.json` 68257 or to `verdict.ts` / `shockPresets.ts` literals. Optional `judge-sheet` test (cut line 2) reads the file in vitest and asserts the worked example figures and the no-dash rule.

### Ordered Implementation Steps (~60 min, cut order marked)

1. **Rewrite `src/lib/judgeMode.ts` + `judgeMode.test.ts`** (20 min): 9-entry registry, `resolveJudgeKey` with `JudgeKeyContext`, modifier policy (`allowShift`, `allowInTextEntry`), reworked `edgeGuard` over `AccountProfile` (delete `GUARD_MIN_ROWS`, `account_prev/next`, the old five flag set), `pickRandomAccount` + `randomAccountPool`, copy tables. Tests: registry shape, context matrix, all 8 flags at boundaries plus the pensioner layoff variant and the defaulted status B/D split, dash scan on all messages, picker determinism with stubbed `rng`, pool predicate (all flags false, income > 0, bills > 0, `runway_state === 'finite'`, deci 20..600, pool non-empty).

All context gathered. Here is the Phase E6 architecture. Two genuine contradictions surfaced (Esc semantics, rehearsal form), so I am asking them first with defaults, and the design below proceeds on those defaults.

## QUESTIONS FOR USER
- Q1: Esc semantics conflict: `consoleStore.ts` documents "Esc clears the lookup query" while the E6 brief says "Esc = clear selection". Recommended default: layered dismiss, Esc cancels an open typed-shock gate first, then clears the lookup query, then resets the whole console (query is already empty at that point, so the last step equals clear selection plus clear twist). This matches the between-judges ritual and needs no new store action.
- Q2: Rehearsal form: an in-app timed dock (small component driving the real console through 5 scripted steps) vs a printed script only (section of the paper sheet). Recommended default: in-app dock with the printed script as the named cut line if the hour runs short (the script data module ships either way).

---

## Architecture: Judge Mode (E6) - Phase 6 of 7

### Overview
E6 turns the console into a live judging instrument: one authoritative keyboard map exported from `src/lib/judgeMode.ts` and wired by a thin window-level adapter hook, an edge-account guard rebuilt to read the E1 profile flags (with contextual copy for the layoff-on-pensioner case), a lean scripted rehearsal dock over 5 frozen golden-fixture accounts, and a one-page printable judge sheet in `public/` as the laptop-dead fallback. All rules stay pure functions in `src/lib`; components only wire listeners and markup, and the adapter fires exactly one existing atomic store action per keystroke.

### Phase Scope
Covers: keyboard shortcuts and their context rules, edge-account guards and operator script lines, rehearsal mode and its data, paper fallback artifact. Connects to: E2 (store actions and DOM seams `id="account-lookup"`, `data-preset`, `type="button"` are consumed, not changed; the reserved key map comment in `consoleStore.ts` is superseded by a pointer to the judgeMode registry), E5 (Atlas above console, `id="atlas"` / `id="console"`; the single window listener works across both sections), E4 (reads `planMath`/`planText`/`PlanCard` for context only, zero edits to those files or README.md), E7 (ReceiptBadge untouched; only a receipt link slot in the bar is possible later). Out of scope: any store action changes, any shock math, any E4 plan content.

### Component Breakdown

| Component | Responsibility | File |
|-----------|---------------|------|
| Key registry + resolver | Single authoritative key table, pure context-aware resolution, modifier policy | `src/lib/judgeMode.ts` (rewrite) |
| Edge guard | Pure guard report from `AccountProfile` flags + live twist context + unknown id | `src/lib/judgeMode.ts` (rework `edgeGuard`) |
| Random account picker | Pure "safe demo" pool and seeded pick for the N key | `src/lib/judgeMode.ts` (new `pickRandomAccount`) |
| Rehearsal script | Pure data: 5 steps over the golden fixture accounts, timer verdict | `src/lib/rehearsal.ts` (new) |
| Dispatcher + key listener | Thin DOM adapter: maps `JudgeAction` to existing store actions and focus effects | `src/components/judge/useJudgeShortcuts.ts` (new) |
| Guard derivation hook | One `useMemo` over `{bundle, selectedId, twist}` calling `edgeGuard`, shared by bar and chips | `src/components/judge/useEdgeGuard.ts` (new) |
| Judge chips | Judge-facing short-label chips near the verdict, full message on hover/aria | `src/components/judge/GuardChips.tsx` (new) |
| Judge bar (extend) | Renders the 9 bindings as buttons via the shared dispatcher; rehearsal toggle; paper sheet link | `src/components/judge/JudgeBar.tsx` (extend) |
| Rehearsal dock | Timed dry run UI: run step, answer button, elapsed vs 2.0 s target | `src/components/judge/RehearsalDock.tsx` (new) |
| App shell | Mounts `useJudgeShortcuts`, `JudgeBar` (bottom), `RehearsalDock` | `src/App.tsx` (extend) |
| Console shell | Mounts `GuardChips` as one new sibling line after `cp-grid` | `src/components/console/ConsoleView.tsx` (one line) |
| Paper sheet | Standalone printable one page: definitions, formula, bands, worked example, guards, keys | `public/judge-sheet.html` (new) |
| Store comment | Reserved key map block replaced by a pointer to `JUDGE_SHORTCUTS` | `src/state/consoleStore.ts` (comment only) |

### Data Flow

```
window keydown (App mounts useJudgeShortcuts once)
  -> adapter: isTextEntry(target)? isComposing? repeat?   (DOM facts only)
  -> resolveJudgeKey(event, context)                      [pure, src/lib/judgeMode.ts]
       context = { inTextEntry, typedGateOpen }
  -> JudgeAction | null
  -> dispatchJudgeAction(action)   (same function serves JudgeBar button clicks)
       twist n      -> useConsole.applyPreset(SHOCK_PRESETS[n-1].id)
       reset_twist  -> useConsole.resetTwist()
       reset_all    -> useConsole.resetAll()
       focus_lookup -> document.getElementById('account-lookup').focus()
       dismiss      -> cancelTypedShock() | setQuery('') | resetAll()   (layered)
       random       -> pickRandomAccount(bundle, {rng}) -> selectAccount(id)
  -> store update (one atomic action per keystroke, E2 contract intact)
  -> ConsoleView derivation useMemo (unchanged: applyTwist, verdictBand, forecast, plan)
  -> useEdgeGuard(): edgeGuard({profile, jobLossActive, knownAccountIds})
       -> GuardChips (chips row under cp-grid) + JudgeBar guard strip (full messages)
RehearsalDock "Run step" -> same store actions (selectAccount + applyPreset), stopwatch local
```

### File Structure

| File | Purpose | Changes |
|------|---------|---------|
| `src/lib/judgeMode.ts` | Registry, resolver, guard, picker, copy tables | Rewrite: 9-binding `JUDGE_SHORTCUTS`, `resolveJudgeKey`, `edgeGuard` over `AccountProfile`, `pickRandomAccount`, delete `GUARD_MIN_ROWS`, `account_prev/next`, old flag set |
| `src/lib/judgeMode.test.ts` | Unit tests | Rewrite to the new registry, context matrix, guard copy, picker determinism |
| `src/lib/rehearsal.ts` | `REHEARSAL_SCRIPT`, `REHEARSAL_TARGET_MS`, `rehearsalVerdict` | New |
| `src/lib/rehearsal.test.ts` | Coverage + artifact pinning | New |
| `src/components/judge/useJudgeShortcuts.ts` | `useJudgeDispatcher`, `useJudgeShortcuts` | New |
| `src/components/judge/useEdgeGuard.ts` | `useEdgeGuard` shared derivation | New |
| `src/components/judge/GuardChips.tsx` | Chip row near verdict | New |
| `src/components/judge/RehearsalDock.tsx` | Timed dry run panel | New |
| `src/components/judge/JudgeBar.tsx` | Bar | Extend: props `onToggleRehearsal`, `rehearsalOpen`, `paperHref`; trailing link + toggle button |
| `src/components/judge/JudgeBar.test.ts` | Bar tests | Extend: 9 bindings, toggle, paper link |
| `src/components/judge/judgeShortcuts.smoke.test.ts` | jsdom adapter smoke (style of `console.smoke.test.ts`) | New |
| `src/App.tsx` | Shell | Extend: `useJudgeShortcuts()`, `<JudgeBar>` bottom bar with `onAction={dispatch}`, `<RehearsalDock>` |
| `src/components/console/ConsoleView.tsx` | Console shell | One line: `<GuardChips guard={useEdgeGuard()} />` after `cp-grid` (or extract to a prop-free child if the E4 merge conflicts) |
| `src/state/consoleStore.ts` | Store | Comment only: reserved map block becomes "see `JUDGE_SHORTCUTS` in src/lib/judgeMode.ts" |
| `public/judge-sheet.html` | Printable fallback | New: standalone inline-CSS one pager |
| `docs/competition-day-runbook.md` | Runbook | Add the sheet link to the Sunday demo row and the "Offline booth" risk fallback cell |
| `docs/judge-sheet.test.ts` (optional, in `src/`) | Asserts sheet numbers | New, cut line 2 |

### Technology Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Why | Alternative Rejected | Trade-off |
|----------|--------|-----|---------------------|-----------|
| Key map source of truth | One `JUDGE_SHORTCUTS` table in `src/lib/judgeMode.ts`; `consoleStore` comment points at it | The brief names judgeMode as owner; one table means the bar, the tests, and the sheet cannot drift | Keeping two maps with a sync comment | The E2 comment wording (Esc, arrows) is superseded; recorded in decisions.md |
| Key set | Exactly the reserved map: `1`-`4`, `r`, `Shift+R`, `/`, `Esc`, `N` (9 bindings) | Reserved map is the approved contract; arrows removed (they conflicted with the map and with text selection via Shift+arrows) | Keeping ArrowLeft/ArrowRight walking | Account browsing loses keyboard stepping; lookup typing and N cover the ritual |
| Modifier policy | Reject ctrl/meta/alt always; `shiftKey` allowed only for bindings with `allowShift` (only `Shift+R`) | Shift alone never triggers browser shortcuts; `Shift+R` needs it; `Shift+4` types `$` so numbers cannot collide | Blanket modifier reject (killed Shift+R) | Caps Lock `R` also fires reset-all; documented, harmless |
| Listener placement | Pure `resolveJudgeKey` in lib + `useJudgeShortcuts` window listener mounted in `App` | Window scope works across Atlas and console (E5 layout); pure rules unit test without DOM; layering holds | Listeners in ConsoleView (misses Atlas focus, remount churn); listeners in the store module (DOM in state layer) | One global listener must own the focus guard carefully |
| Typed-shock interplay | While `typedStatus` is `reading` or `pending`, only `Esc` resolves; text-entry focus suppresses everything except `Esc` | `applyPreset` would silently `retireTypedParse` and drop the judge's sentence chips; typing `1` in the lookup is an id digit, not a shortcut | Allowing resets during the gate | The confirm button is auto-focused (a button), so the gate-open rule is required, not just the focus rule |
| Guard source | Read `profile.flags` (E1 artifact) instead of re-deriving thresholds | E1 flags are verified field-by-field by `scripts/engine/verify.py`; kills the dead `GUARD_MIN_ROWS = 6` and its wrong message | Keeping `rowCount < 18` re-derivation in TS | Guard trusts the artifact; drift is caught by the existing engine verify, not duplicated in TS |
| Guard placement | Full messages in the judge-facing `JudgeBar` strip (operator), short chips near the verdict (`GuardChips`) | Operator needs the sentence, judges need the glance; two renders of one pure `GuardReport` via `useEdgeGuard` | Chips inside ShockPanel/PlanCard (merge risk with E4) | Chips sit under `cp-grid`, a few pixels from the badge rather than inside it |
| N picker | Pure `pickRandomAccount` with a "safe demo" pool, injectable `rng` | Never embarrasses the operator; deterministic under test and rehearsal | Uniform random over 4500 ids | Extreme accounts are unreachable via N (still typed by judges, guarded) |
| Rehearsal | Pure `rehearsal.ts` script + lean `RehearsalDock` with stopwatch | The live ritual is timing muscle memory; the data module survives the UI cut | Full game-like scoring, persistence | No history or scoring beyond a per-step green/amber/red label |
| Paper fallback | `public/judge-sheet.html`, standalone, `@media print`, linked from the runbook | Ships with Pages, prints offline, needs no build step; runbook "Offline booth" row expects everything bundled | `docs/` markdown (not printable to one page without tooling); generated PDF in repo (binary churn) | Hand-copied numbers from `golden_fixtures.json`; an optional test pins them |

### Interfaces

### Authoritative Key Table (ships in the bar, the sheet, and the tests)

| Key | event.key | Action | Effect | Context rules |
|-----|-----------|--------|--------|---------------|
| `1` | `1` | twist preset 1 | `applyPreset('layoff')` | Suppressed in text entry and while the typed gate is open |
| `2` | `2` | twist preset 2 | `applyPreset('cost_spike')` | Same |
| `3` | `3` | twist preset 3 | `applyPreset('emergency_repair')` | Same |
| `4` | `4` | twist preset 4 | `applyPreset('combo')` | Same |
| `r` | `r` | reset twist, keep account | `resetTwist()` | Same |
| `Shift+R` | `R` | reset everything | `resetAll()` | Same; the only binding tolerating shift. Caps Lock `R` also fires it |
| `/` | `/` | focus lookup | `#account-lookup`.focus(), preventDefault (Firefox quick find) | Suppressed in text entry and while the gate is open |
| `Esc` | `Escape` | layered dismiss | gate open: `cancelTypedShock()`; else query non-empty: `setQuery('')` (+ blur); else selected or shocked: `resetAll()`; else no-op | Active everywhere, including text entry (the only key exempt from the focus guard) |
| `N` | `n` | pseudo-random account | `selectAccount(pickRandomAccount(bundle))` | Suppressed in text entry and while the gate is open; key repeat ignored |

Esc layered rule (the Q1 default): it dismisses the innermost layer first, so the operator can never lose a typed sentence to a stray keypress, and between judges two presses (or one when no query) return the console to the empty state. This supersedes the `consoleStore` comment wording.

### Guard Copy Table (no dash glyphs anywhere)

| Flag id | Fires when | Chip label | Operator message (bar) | Operator script line (rehearsal) |
|---------|-----------|------------|------------------------|----------------------------------|
| `unknown_account` | id missing or not in `bundle.byId` | unknown id | Account id is not in the loaded profile set | "That id is not in the 4,500 account index, let me retype it." |
| `pensioner` (idle) | `flags.pensioner` | pension income | Pension income account: money in is pension, not wages | "Income here is pension, so the money in line reads differently." |
| `pensioner` (layoff twist live) | `flags.pensioner && twist.jobLoss` | pension vs layoff | Layoff twist simulated against pension income: this account has no wage to lose, read the verdict as a stress test | "Good catch: this customer's income is pension, so the layoff card is a stress test on fixed income. Their real risk is bills up, not job loss." |
| `zero_income` | `flags.zero_income` | zero income | Zero income: money in is 0, so the layoff and EI framing does not apply | "Money in is zero here, so I read the shock as a spending side stress." |
| `thin_history` | `flags.thin_history` (row_count under 18, E1 definition) | thin history | Thin history: fewer than 18 monthly rows, so the baseline medians rest on a short window | "Short history, so I treat the baseline as low confidence." |
| `negative_buffer` | `flags.negative_buffer` | negative buffer | Savings buffer is below zero: the baseline already reads 0.0 months of runway | "Buffer is already below zero, so the plan is recovery first." |
| `defaulted_loan` | `flags.defaulted_loan`, message varies on `loan.status` | defaulted loan | status D: Loan in arrears (status D): the account still pays a loan it is behind on. status B: Loan defaulted and closed (status B): no payment runs, so the loan levers do not apply | D: "This loan is running and in arrears, so deferral is exactly the intervention." B: "This loan already defaulted and closed, so there is no payment to defer." |
| `no_loan` | `loan_payment_cents === 0` | no loan | No running loan payment: the loan deferral lever does not apply | "No loan payment here, so I skip the loan lever and say why." |
| `zero_household_bills` | `household_bills_cents === 0` | zero bills | Household bills are 0: a bills shock cannot move this account | "Bills are zero here, so a rent shock cannot land; I would swap to the repair card." |

Rules: flags are advice, never gates (`selectAccount` accepts any known id regardless of flags, the hard constraint "any account must work" is untouched). Canonical order is `GUARD_FLAG_ORDER`, the pensioner message variant is decided by the live twist, and every message keeps the repo no-dash content rule (a `judgeMode.test.ts` case already scans for dash code points; keep it). This table backs the shipped `docs/devpost.md` claim: thin history, negative buffer, zero bills, and missing loans all flag before a judge finds them.

### Rehearsal Spec

Format: scripted dry run, 5 steps, timed, no stakes, driven through the real store so the operator practices the actual keystrokes. Target: 2.0 s from step reveal to "Answered" click (`REHEARSAL_TARGET_MS`); labels `fast` / `ok` / `slow` at 2 s / 4 s.

| Step | Account | Why this account | Twist | Expected flags | Expected read |
|------|---------|------------------|-------|----------------|---------------|
| 1 | `68257` | Golden fixture: odd median, running loan C, clean | `layoff` (1) | none | Fair skies 9.8 months falls to Storm warning 1.8 months |
| 2 | `23838` | Golden fixture: half cent tie in I, `no_shortfall` branch | `cost_spike` (2) | none | Verdict stays Clear, buffer absorbs |
| 3 | `98952` | Golden fixture: pensioner, no loan | `layoff` (1) | `pensioner` (layoff variant), `no_loan` | Stress-test framing, loan lever skipped |
| 4 | `49900` | Golden fixture: thin history (17 rows) and zero income | `combo` (4) | `thin_history`, `zero_income` | Caveat spoken before the number |
| 5 | `42988` | Golden fixture: defaulted loan status D, negative buffer | `emergency_repair` (3) | `defaulted_loan` (D variant), `negative_buffer` | Baseline already 0.0, recovery plan |

Coverage: all five E1 flags fire at least once, all four presets fire once except `layoff` (twice, needed for the pensioner variant), every runway branch appears across the fixtures. Candidate selection criteria (recorded for any future re-pick): ids come from `scripts/engine/golden_fixtures.json`, which is hand-verified and pinned by both pytest and vitest; `rehearsal.test.ts` asserts each step's id exists in the shipped `profiles.json` with exactly the expected flags, so artifact drift fails a test and names the step. If a rebuild ever invalidates an id, re-pick from `meta.edge_flag_counts` smallest buckets first (`zero_income` 14, `negative_buffer` 23, `defaulted_loan` 45, `thin_history` 377, `pensioner` 740), preferring fixture-frozen ids so the paper sheet example stays pinned.

UI (`RehearsalDock`): opened from a toggle in `JudgeBar`; shows step n of 5, the judge card sentence (from `presetById`), the script line, a "Run step" button (selects the account and applies the preset via the store), and an "Answered" button that stops the stopwatch and prints the verdict label. Closing resets the counter. No persistence, no network, no score history.

Cut line (Q2 default): if the hour runs short, cut `RehearsalDock.tsx` and keep `rehearsal.ts` plus a printed script block in the judge sheet. The data module is cheap and the sheet prints it.

### Paper Fallback Spec (`public/judge-sheet.html`)

Purpose: the rehearsed fallback when the laptop dies or the venue network stalls (runbook risk table "Offline booth" expects everything bundled locally with fixture labels; `docs/devpost.md` promises a graceful fallback). Standalone HTML, inline CSS, `@media print` sized to one US Letter page, no build step, no JS. Linked from `docs/competition-day-runbook.md` (Sunday demo row and the Offline booth fallback cell) and printable from the live site (`/judge-sheet.html`). Readme linking is deliberately out of scope (concurrent agent owns README.md).

Sections, in order:
1. **Header**: "Resilience Weather Station, judge sheet", competition name, "synthetic demo data label applies to cached fixture figures".
2. **The six definitions**: I, F, S, B, H, P exactly as `docs/tangerine-challenge.md` lines 52 to 59.
3. **Runway formula and rounding**: the branch formula (challenge doc lines 63 to 69), ROUND_HALF_UP to 1 decimal, cap at 120.0.
4. **Worked example** (numbers hand-copied from `scripts/engine/golden_fixtures.json` account `68257`, whose "steps" block is visible workings): I = 650,326c, S = 716,084c, B = 643,785c, H = 430,672c, P = 284,493c, gap = 65,758c, baseline deci = (20 x 643785 + 65758) // (2 x 65758) = 98, so 9.8 months. Layoff card: income_after = round(0.55 x I) = 357,679c, gap_after = 716,084 - 357,679 = 358,405c, deci = (20 x 643785 + 358405) // (2 x 358405) = 18, so 1.8 months. Fair skies becomes Storm warning.
5. **Verdict bands**: the five `verdict.ts` bands with their threshold strings (critical: buffer gone or under 1.0 month; storm warning 1.0 to 2.9; watch 3.0 to 5.9; fair skies 6.0 to 11.9; clear 12.0 and up or no shortfall).
6. **Twist card arithmetic**: `income_after = 0.55 x I` (layoff), `spending_after = S + 0.15 x H` (bills up 15%), `one_off_costs = 1.0 x S` (furnace), combo is layoff plus bills; duration is display only.
7. **Guard one-liners**: the chip labels plus one phrase each from the guard copy table.
8. **Key table**: the authoritative 9 rows.
9. **Rehearsal script**: the 5 steps (account, card, expected flags), so the drill survives a dead laptop.

Content rules: no em dash, en dash, minus sign, or double hyphen anywhere (use `x`, `+`, and words); money shown in cents and dollars; every figure traceable to `golden_fixtures.json` 68257 or to `verdict.ts` / `shockPresets.ts` literals. ```
## Judge mode (E6)

One authoritative keyboard table (JUDGE_SHORTCUTS in
src/lib/judgeMode.ts) drives the bar, the tests, and the printable
judge sheet: 1 to 4 apply the twist presets, r resets the twist,
Shift + R resets everything, slash focuses the account lookup, Esc
dismisses layer by layer (typed gate, then query, then the whole
console), N opens a pseudo-random safe demo account. A window level
adapter (src/components/judge/useJudgeShortcuts.ts) owns the DOM
facts (text entry focus, typed gate open, key repeat) and fires
exactly one existing consoleStore action per keystroke; all rules
stay pure and unit tested in src/lib.

Edge guards read the E1 profile flags plus two numeric rules (no
running loan, zero household bills) and one contextual rule (pensioner
under a live layoff twist): they inform the operator in the judge bar
and the judges as chips near the verdict, and they never block an
account selection. Rehearsal is a timed five step dry run over the
golden fixture accounts (src/lib/rehearsal.ts, RehearsalDock), and
public/judge-sheet.html is the one page printable fallback (formula,
verdict bands, worked example from fixture 68257, twist arithmetic,
guards, keys) linked from the competition day runbook.
```

### `docs/decisions.md` entry (append)

```
## Nov 07 2026, Phase E6: Judge mode key map, guard contract, rehearsal, paper fallback

**Context**: the judgeMode scaffold registry (1 to 3, 0, arrows) contradicted the E2 reserved key map, its GUARD_MIN_ROWS = 6 guard could never fire on real data (minimum 12 rows, E1 defines thin_history below 18), and rehearsal plus paper fallback were missing. Esc semantics differed between the store comment (clear query) and the brief (clear selection).

**Decision**: JUDGE_SHORTCUTS in src/lib/judgeMode.ts is the single key table (1 to 4 presets, r reset twist, Shift + R reset all, slash focus lookup, Esc layered dismiss: typed gate then query then resetAll, N pseudo-random safe account); the consoleStore comment points to it. Guards read profile.flags directly (five E1 flags plus no_loan, zero_household_bills, and a pensioner variant under a live layoff twist), copy per flag is fixed in the guard table, guards inform and never gate. Rehearsal is a five step timed dry run over golden fixture accounts (68257, 23838, 98952, 49900, 42988) covering every flag and preset; N draws from a safe demo pool (no flags, income and bills above zero, finite runway) with an injectable rng. Paper fallback is public/judge-sheet.html, a standalone one page print sheet linked from the runbook.

**Rationale**: one table removes the drift class entirely; reading E1 flags keeps one verified source for the thresholds and kills the dead guard; fixture-frozen rehearsal ids are pinned by tests on both sides of the language boundary; the printed sheet answers the runbook offline-booth rule.

**Trade-offs**: arrow key account walking is dropped (lookup and N cover the ritual); Caps Lock R also fires reset all (documented); the confirm-gate suppression means shortcuts are dead while typed chips are open (only Esc works); RehearsalDock UI is the named cut line if the hour runs short, keeping the script data and the printed sheet.
```

Note for other agents (knowledge sharing): the pattern "pure registry in `src/lib`, one window adapter hook in `src/components/judge`, one dispatcher shared by keyboard and click paths" is reusable for any future global shortcut; the `typedGateOpen` context rule is the reference for keeping the Gemini confirm gate safe from future key work.

## Nov 07 2026, Phase E6: Judge mode key map, guard contract, rehearsal, paper fallback

**Context**: the judgeMode scaffold registry (1 to 3, 0, arrows)
contradicted the E2 reserved key map, its GUARD_MIN_ROWS = 6 guard
could never fire on real data (minimum 12 rows, E1 defines thin_history
below 18), and rehearsal plus paper fallback were missing. Esc
semantics differed between the store comment (clear query) and the
plan (clear selection).

**Decision**: JUDGE_SHORTCUTS in src/lib/judgeMode.ts is the single key
table (1 to 4 presets, r reset twist, Shift + R reset all, slash focus
lookup, Esc layered dismiss: typed gate, then query, then resetAll, N
pseudo-random safe account); the consoleStore comment points to it.
Layered Esc is user confirmed. Guards read profile.flags directly
(five E1 flags plus no_loan, zero_household_bills, and a pensioner
variant under a live layoff twist), copy per flag is fixed in the
guard table, guards inform and never gate. Rehearsal is a five step
timed dry run over golden fixture accounts (68257, 23838, 98952,
49900, 42988) covering every flag and preset, shipped as an in-app
dock (user confirmed; the printed script ships in the paper sheet
either way and the dock UI is the named cut line). N draws from a safe
demo pool (no flags, income and bills above zero, finite runway) with
an injectable rng. Paper fallback is public/judge-sheet.html, a
standalone one page print sheet linked from the runbook.

**Rationale**: one table removes the drift class entirely; reading E1
flags keeps one verified source for the thresholds and kills the dead
guard; fixture-frozen rehearsal ids are pinned by tests on both sides
of the language boundary; the printed sheet answers the runbook
offline booth rule.

**Trade-offs**: arrow key account walking is dropped (lookup and N
cover the ritual); Caps Lock R also fires reset all (documented); the
confirm gate suppression means shortcuts are dead while typed chips
are open (only Esc works); RehearsalDock UI is the cut line if time
runs short.

<subagent sessionID="ses_e469d515effeETWklCvhooYEIO" state="completed" description="Implement E5 Storm Atlas">
All gates green. Final report:

## QUESTIONS FOR USER
- Q1: `capBin` semantics were not defined in the design. I shipped it as the overflow `AtlasBin` object (`bins[5]`, `.overflow === true`), so the view can read `plot.capBin.count` without indexing. Confirm, or say if it should be a count.
- Q2: The design's example headline numbers (34% baseline, 61% under laid off) do not exist in the shipped artifact under the specified bands. With `DEFAULT_HEADLINE_BANDS = ['critical','storm_warning']` the real values are 1% baseline (60 of 4,500) and 10% under laid off (435 of 4,500). I implemented the specified sentence spec and bands, and pinned the real numbers in tests. Confirm the threshold is still "under 3 months", or name the band set that produces the intended headline.
- Q3: `StormAtlas` receives `selectedId` but the design never says what it renders. I ship a small "Tracking account N" chip in the subline row (the band cell cannot be marked without the entries). Confirm or specify.

## Frontend Implementation: Phase E5 Storm Atlas

### Design Plan
- **Palette** (existing console tokens, one source): `#ff6a4d` cp-critical, `#f4b740` cp-storm, `#8b7cf6` cp-watch, `#39c2e0` cp-fair, `#35d0ae` cp-clear, ground `#070c18` with `#e9effa` paper ink.
- **Typography**: display `ui-monospace` stack (headline, counts, tabular numerals), body `system-ui` (caption, notes), utility mono uppercase with 0.1em tracking (labels, ticks).
- **Layout**: one panel (`ax-shell`) holding headline, subline, five band cells (auto-fit grid, 44px min), then a full width `960x240` SVG strip plot with a hanging histogram silhouette, tinted segment columns, dot field, axis and month ticks.
- **ASCII wireframe**:
```
+----------------------------------------------------------+
| 10% of accounts would have under 3 months of runway ...  |  headline (largest type)
| 435 of 4,500 accounts   At baseline: 1% (60 of 4,500)   |  subline
| [⛈ Critical][🌧 Storm][☁ Watch][⛅ Fair][☀ Clear]        |  redundant encoding cells
| [tinted segments + silhouette bars + 4,500 dots]         |  signature strip plot
| 0  1  3  6  12  120  120+  (months)                     |
| Every dot is one account. Axis segments follow ...       |  caption
+----------------------------------------------------------+
```
- **Signature element**: the 4,500 dot strip plot on a piecewise axis (each sixth of the width is one band edge, so the under-3-month window is 1/6 of the picture, not a sliver), tinted by the same `--cp-band` tokens the console badge uses.

### Staged implementation (each stage written and verified green before the next)

| Stage | Files | Targeted result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Fold | deleted `src/lib/weatherState.ts` (257 lines), `src/lib/weatherState.test.ts` (351 lines) | exactly 2 files red: `src/lib/stormAtlas.test.ts`, `src/components/atlas/StormAtlas.test.ts`; 426 tests passed elsewhere |
| 2 stormAtlas | `src/lib/stormAtlas.ts` rewrite, `src/lib/stormAtlas.test.ts` rewrite | 18 passed |
| 3 atlasPlot | `src/lib/atlasPlot.ts` new, `src/lib/atlasPlot.test.ts` new | 13 passed (14 after the segment tint assertion added in stage 5) |
| 4 StormAtlas | `src/components/atlas/StormAtlas.tsx` rewrite, `StormAtlas.test.ts` rewrite | 6 passed |
| 5 strip plot | `src/components/atlas/AtlasStripPlot.tsx` new, `AtlasStripPlot.test.ts` new, plus `ATLAS_BIN_BANDS` export in `atlasPlot.ts` | 7 passed |
| 6 section + css | `src/components/atlas/AtlasSection.tsx` new, `AtlasSection.test.ts` new, `src/components/atlas/atlas.css` new, `weather.css` wx-atlas block removed (lines 399 to 514), `import './atlas.css'` added to all three atlas components | 8 passed |
| 7 App mount | `src/App.tsx` (`<section id="atlas">` above `<div id="console">`, flex gap on main) | `app.smoke.test.ts` passed unchanged, 3 tests |
| 8 scan + gates | `src/dashScan.test.ts` (registered `stormAtlas.ts/.test`, `atlasPlot.ts/.test`, AUTO_DIRS `src/components/atlas`, CSS_FILES `atlas.css`, coverage assertions, E5 wording) | 3 passed, then full gates below |

### Fold confirmation
```
grep -rn "weatherState" src/
  src/components/weather/WeatherBands.test.ts:13   (comment, allowed)
  src/components/weather/WeatherBands.test.ts:84   (the source guard, allowed)
  src/lib/stormAtlas.ts:22                         (comment saying it is deleted)
  src/lib/forecast.ts:34                           (pre-existing comment; forecast* is do-not-touch)
```
No imports remain. `grep -rn "wx-atlas" src/` returns nothing. The negative buffer to flood and drought ratio branches went with the deleted file; `verdictBand` is the only ladder.

### Conservation and honesty results
- `stormAtlas.test.ts`: 5 band fixture (2/2/2/2/2 of 10), percents 20 each, thirds fixture proves percents may sum to 99, exact sentences for empty (`No accounts in the atlas yet`), zero count, baseline verb `have`, scenario verb `would have`, `At baseline` subline source, `accountsInBand` in caller order.
- Honesty: `shockedAtlasScenario(IDLE)` entries deep equal the recorded baseline for all 4,500 rows (0 mismatches); every preset twist yields `under the <label lowercase> twist` AND at least one row that differs from baseline (layoff 4,231 rows, cost spike 1,212, repair 1,080, combo 4,282); unmatched twists read `under the custom twist`; the layoff headline is asserted equal to its own computed percent plus the label, with `headlineCount > baseline`.
- `atlasPlot.test.ts`: golden `jitterFor('68257') = 2756683695 / 4294967296` (= 0.6418404390569776), boundary table 9/10/29/30/59/60/119/120/1199/1200 to bins 0..5, cap bin collects `finite 1200` and `no_shortfall 1200` (2 dots, spread apart, inside segment six), clamping of -50, 5000, NaN, Infinity, shipped artifact: 4,500 dots, every id exactly once, bin sums 4,500, `countsByBand` sums equal each bin count, dot band totals identical to `summarizeStormAtlas` counts.
- `AtlasSection.test.ts`: baseline `1% ... at baseline` with `60 of 4,500`, 4,500 circles, storm dots 26; after `applyPreset('layoff')` the field re colors (storm dots 26 to 384, critical 34 to 51) with `10% ... would have ... under the laid off twist`, `435 of 4,500`, `At baseline: 1% (60 of 4,500)`.

### Gate outputs
```
npx vitest run                      Test Files 44 passed (44)   Tests 479 passed (479)
npm run typecheck                   tsc --noEmit  (clean)
npm run build                       tsc build + vite build, 63 modules, dist assets written
uv run pytest -q                    160 passed in 3.78s
uv run python -m scripts.engine.verify
  artifact sha256 9ec428bf...   drift: none   scripts.engine.verify: PASS
```
466 baseline tests plus the new atlas tests, minus the 17 tests that lived in the two deleted weatherState files, all green.

### consoleStore zero-diff proof
```
git diff --stat src/state/consoleStore.ts     (empty)
git status --porcelain  ->  no src/state entry at all
```
Drill down goes through the existing `selectAccount` action only; `AtlasSection.test.ts` also greps `consoleStore.ts` for `atlas` and `Atlas` (both absent) and checks 14 E2 to E4 sources for atlas imports.

### Perf note
Measured on this machine with a temporary bench (deleted after): one twist change over 4,500 profiles runs `shockedAtlasScenario` in 0.53 ms and `summarize` (twisted) + `shockedAtlasScenario(IDLE)` + `summarize` (baseline) + `buildAtlasPlot` in 1.37 ms, 1.90 ms total, warm. The design's 2 to 5 ms estimate holds. Frame time for reconciling 4,500 keyed circles could not be measured: this checkout has no browser automation, so no 8x throttle drag frame was captured. The single path per band fallback is therefore NOT applied and is documented in the `AtlasStripPlot` header comment with the 50 ms trigger and the measurement gap stated honestly.

### Deviations and notes
1. `capBin`, `selectedId` rendering, and the example percentages are flagged in the questions above; all three are shipped best-effort and green.
2. `import './atlas.css'` was deferred from stages 4 and 5 to stage 6 (the stylesheet did not exist yet, and a missing CSS import fails module resolution in vitest), then added to all three components in stage 6 as the stage list assigns.
3. Keyboard access to a dot: the plot is `role="img"` per the design, so dots are mouse targets; the console lookup is the keyboard path and the component comment says so.
4. Mobile: the SVG scales with the viewport, so tick text shrinks below legibility on very narrow screens (same characteristic as the E3 forecast strip); headline, cells, subline, and caption are HTML and stay full size.
5. Untouched but noticed: `src/lib/forecast.ts` line 34 still says weatherState is "quarantined (E5 rework pending)", which is now stale. `forecast*` is do-not-touch, so it needs an orchestrator decision.
6. `README.md` and `docs/decisions.md` show as modified in `git status`. Those edits are from a concurrent session (an E6 judge mode decision entry and an Entire README sentence), not from E5; E5 touched only the files in the stage table.

### Components modified
| File | Component | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `src/lib/stormAtlas.ts` | summarize, shockedAtlasScenario, accountsInBand, entryBand | band counting, honest scenario wording |
| `src/lib/atlasPlot.ts` | buildAtlasPlot, jitterFor, binIndexFor | piecewise axis geometry, deterministic dots |
| `src/components/atlas/StormAtlas.tsx` | headline panel | headline, subline, five band cells |
| `src/components/atlas/AtlasStripPlot.tsx` | strip plot | 4,500 dots, silhouette, ticks, ring, drill click |
| `src/components/atlas/AtlasSection.tsx` | section shell | one useMemo derivation, loading/error notes, scroll to console |
| `src/components/atlas/atlas.css` | ax- styles | band mapping, panel, plot, cells |
| `src/components/weather/weather.css` | (trimmed) | wx-atlas block removed |
| `src/App.tsx` | shell | mounts `#atlas` above `#console` |
| `src/dashScan.test.ts` | content rule | registers E5 files and stylesheet |

### Verification Checklist
- [x] Design follows frontend-design skill principles (band vocabulary from the domain, headline as thesis, structure encodes the band edges)
- [x] Distinctive, not templated (piecewise band axis and hanging silhouette, not a generic bar chart)
- [x] Responsive down to mobile (auto-fit cells, clamped headline, wrapping subline, scaling SVG)
- [x] Visible keyboard focus (no new focusable controls; existing controls untouched)
- [x] Reduced motion respected (`scrollIntoView` swaps smooth for auto, zero animation in the section)
- [x] Accessibility (semantic list and figure, `role="img"` with headline as accessible name, glyph plus label plus count plus number redundant encoding, AA contrast on reused tokens)
- [x] No em dashes, double hyphens, or dash equivalents in new strings and comments (dashScan covers all new files and atlas.css)
- [x] Build succeeds (`npm run build`, typecheck, 479 tests, 160 pytest, engine verify PASS)
</subagent>

content.text:
E5 completed, all gates green (479 vitest, 160 pytest). Three questions:

Q1: capBin semantics (object vs count) — trivial implementation detail; object is fine (view reads .count). I could answer myself as orchestrator judgment? It's a design contract detail; default (object) shipped. I can confirm without user — but it's posed to user. Minor; I'll fold into a question with Q2 (which matters) and Q3.

Q2: IMPORTANT — headline numbers: with critical+storm_warning (under 3 months), real baseline = 1% (60 of 4500), laid off = 10% (435). The design's example 34%/61% don't exist. Question: confirm under-3-months threshold (1% baseline) or pick another band set for a punchier pitch headline. This is a genuine pitch-quality question: 1% baseline is a weak pitch finding ("1% of accounts have under 3 months"), while under 6 months (watch included) might be bigger. Let me compute... unknown without data. The user picked "under 3 months" earlier. Now real numbers show 1% baseline / 10% under layoff. For a pitch, "under 6 months" might be ~5-8%? unknown. Could offer: keep under 3 months (1%→10%, a 10x story: "a layoff takes the at-risk population from 1% to 10%") vs under 6 months (bigger base number). Actually the 1%→10% delta IS a compelling story ("the twist puts 435 accounts in the storm zone vs 60 at baseline"). I should present the real numbers and let user choose.

Q3: selectedId rendering — "Tracking account N" chip. Fine, confirm.

Also noted: forecast.ts:34 stale comment (weatherState quarantined, E5 rework pending) — needs a tiny comment fix; can fold into E6 pass step 0 (with the planText 6x fix).

Next step: E5 code review (per lifecycle). Launch review now; relay Q2 meanwhile? Review is independent of the headline choice (sentence spec already pinned by tests; changing DEFAULT_HEADLINE_BANDS is a constant + test change). //
